speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To better understand your condition, could you tell me if you have experienced any recent unintentional weight loss or changes in your bowel habits? Additionally, have you noticed any pain or tenderness in your abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the shortness of breath and large ovarian mass, I need to rule out pleural effusion. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any abdominal pain or bloating, and have you noticed any nausea or early satiety when eating? I will also request an ultrasound of the pelvis to further characterize the ovarian mass.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Shortness of breath. I also have Increased abdominal girth, Fatigue, No significant weight loss or gain.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: CA-125.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Ultrasound: Large mass in the right ovary, significant ascites present. CA-125: Normal

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a large ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion with a normal CA-125 is highly suggestive of Meigs syndrome, likely secondary to an ovarian fibroma. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol regularly. Works as a high school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that additional history. Do you have any family history of ovarian or breast cancer? I also need to confirm if you have experienced any palpitations or swelling in your legs.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical triad of a solid ovarian mass, ascites, and pleural effusion, combined with a normal CA-125 level, strongly points to Meigs syndrome. I am confident in this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
